intended_object: For a right ideal I of the endomorphism ring End_R(M), the submodule I·M = Σ_{f∈I} f(M) of M, i.e. the submodule generated by the images of all endomorphisms in I. When I = eEnd(M) is complemented, this equals e(M). Inferred from the docstring and the lemmas about it in the file.
explanation: A `Submodule (End R M)ᵐᵒᵖ (End R M)` is a right ideal of End R M, since `op a • b = b * a`. The body takes the supremum of `range f` over all f in I. That is exactly the submodule Σ_{f∈I} f(M), which is the same as I·M = {Σ f_i(m_i)}. The library proves that for a complemented right ideal this equals the range of the projection idempotent, as the docstring says, so the definition and its documentation agree. Mathlib's `Submodule.smul` (`I • N`) covers left ideals of the scalar ring, not right ideals of the endomorphism ring acting on M, so Mathlib has no direct counterpart. Assuming a `Ring` and an `AddCommGroup` instead of a semiring is a minor restriction and fits the setting of projective modules. It does not make the definition too narrow in any meaningful sense.
